text:
Predicates:
TallerThan(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
CanBlock(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jumps(x) ::: x jumps when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Michael ::: a specific individual.
Windy ::: a specific individual.
Peter ::: a specific individual.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (TallerThan(x, y) → CanBlock(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another man, the taller one can block the other's shooting.
TallerThan(Michael, y) for all y in class ::: Michael is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((TallerThan(x, y) ∧ TallerThan(y, z)) → TallerThan(x, z)) ::: If x is taller than y and y is taller than z, then x is taller than z.
TallerThan(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
∀x (CanBlock(x, Windy) → ¬Jumps(x)) ::: Michael can block any shooting unless the shooter jumps.
Jumps(Windy) ::: Windy jumps when shooting.
∀x (Jumps(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Every shooter who jumps when shooting is a great shooter.
Conclusion:
¬CanBlock(Windy, Windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
